second_order: remembering and expecting yearly April Fools fun
theme_note: Participants recall earlier subreddit jokes and anticipate another yearly performance.
Participants invent absurd announcements, changes, and roles for the community after company action is denied.

second_order: measuring jokes against MCC salt and backlash
theme_note: Participants judge what joking can land by invoking backlash and continuing anger over MCC.

second_order: getting the Chief onto the canvas and signing it r/halo
theme_note: Participants recruit help, build a Chief, add the room name, and celebrate it as shared work.

second_order: giving up a second Chief under rainbow and VOID pressure
theme_note: A separate coordinate attempt works around larger neighbours, asks about their coordination, and is abandoned when outnumbered.
Participants correct mistaken colours, name attacks, recruit defenders, and celebrate or renew repair work.

second_order: expanding and reshaping the Halo picture
theme_note: Participants propose adjacent Spartans, altered signs, and extensions beyond the first Chief.

second_order: working out peace with pony neighbours
theme_note: Hostile expansion talk, restraint, neighbour help, and treaty language together work out how adjacent Halo and pony art can coexist.

second_order: putting on separate April Fools jokes
theme_note: Participants publish fake announcements, mark them as jokes, enjoy them, and stage a mock subreddit war apart from the canvas work.

second_order: arguing over the right star detail
theme_note: People dispute how a star on the canvas should be repaired; they share the same object but disagree over its proper form.

second_order: playing along with and judging the subreddit prank
theme_note: People recognise, fall for, object to, enjoy, or remember the subreddit’s own April Fools performance; what varies is whether they treat the trick as clever, cruel, convincing, or nostalgic.

second_order: posting canvas calls under low-effort moderation
theme_note: People post a concrete canvas coordinate call and moderators remove it under the ordinary low-effort rule; the call and its local disposition are both part of this practice.

second_order: building Red Spartan after losing Blue Spartan
theme_note: People answer the reported loss of Blue Spartan by starting, laying out, and reimagining Red Spartan; proposals vary from a replacement to a half-red, half-blue memorial.

second_order: arguing whether to put Fix MCC on the picture
theme_note: People use repair talk to press #FixMCC while others insist MCC is already fixed; later codes vary between complaint, joke, compromise, and opposition.
A participant answers reported damage by blaming another group and proposing to rewrite its work, a retaliatory practice distinct from repairing Halo art.

second_order: questioning whether a few pixels are taking over the subreddit
theme_note: A participant challenges how much attention the canvas is receiving, shifting from work on the picture to whether the room has become devoted to it.

second_order: watching placement end and showing the final image
theme_note: People ask when pixel placement will end, congratulate builders when it closes, and post the final image; what varies is anticipation, recognition of closure, and retrospective display.

second_order: turning mistaken vandalism into help through visible plans
theme_note: People initially undo unfamiliar additions, then stop reverting and help once a builder explains the image or shares a plan; what varies is recognition through words, a template, or enough visible pixels.
People warn about bots or ask whether the final work used a script; the record varies from a body-less warning to an explicit denial, so it records concern rather than established automation.
